subject: check-branch-collision refuses every push from a card worktree, because it reads the checked-out branch and finds Hydrostat's own claim ref
activeForm: Teaching check-branch-collision about pushed refs and Hydrostat claims

origin.evidence: cd ~/worktrees/sentiment-analyzer-gsk/card-<id> && git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/some-other-branch  # prints ORPHAN BRANCH DETECTED for card-<id>

work_items: Card #22: make check-branch-collision judge the refs being pushed, not the checked-out branch
runConfiguration.backwards_compatibility: Keep the manual run working: ./scripts/check-branch-collision.sh with no pre-push context still checks the checked-out branch.
runConfiguration.security_tier: low: local pre-push guard, no secrets, no AWS resources, no new CI gate.
runConfiguration.operational_rigour: standard: tests run real git against a local bare origin with only gh stubbed, a mutant proves they bind, make validate green.

description: Found by card #17 on 2026-10-14. scripts/check-branch-collision.sh (pre-push stage) takes BRANCH from git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD and refuses when origin has that branch with no PR. In a card worktree the checked-out branch is card-<id>, and origin/card-<id> always exists as Hydrostat's claim ref with no PR, so every push from a card worktree is refused as an orphan, including a refspec push to a different remote branch (git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/card-17-frontend-ci). The hook never reads the pushed refs, which git supplies on the pre-push hook's stdin. Card #17 worked around it with a temporary worktree checked out on the target branch name. Fix: read local_ref remote_ref pairs from stdin and check each remote_ref; treat refs/heads/card-<n> claim refs as known. Decision: the hook reads PRE_COMMIT_REMOTE_BRANCH, not stdin. pre-commit (4.5.1 measured, pre_commit/commands/hook_impl.py _pre_push_ns) consumes git's pre-push stdin and exports the first ref carrying commits the remote lacks, so stdin is empty by the time the script runs. A manual run still judges the checked-out branch. card-<n> passes as a claim ref, and the remote lookup matches refs/heads/<branch> exactly.
